rules.law_name: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing Ordinance
rules.citation: San Diego Municipal Code Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 11, sections 98.1101, 98.1102, 98.1103, and 98.1104
rules.effective_date_basis: This Ordinance will take effect and be in force on the thirtieth day from and after its final passage.
rules.title: Ban on sale, licensing, and use of automated rent-setting algorithmic devices
rules.requirement: The proposed ordinance would make it unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord, and unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property in San Diego. Tenants could sue landlords for injunctive relief, damages, civil penalties, costs, and reasonable attorney’s fees.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each residential rental property can be a separate violation for landlord use

coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies to 'residential rental property' as defined in San Diego Municipal Code section 98.0702; the document does not reproduce that definition.
coverage.summary: Applies citywide to landlords and residential rental property in the City of San Diego, and to persons selling, licensing, or providing covered algorithmic devices to landlords.

rules.exemptions: Algorithmic device does not include software or products used to publish reports on rental rates or occupancy levels from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old, or from public information, if they do not recommend future rental rates or occupancy levels; it also excludes software or products used to establish rental rates or income limits under local, state, or federal affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.penalty: A tenant may seek injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation against a landlord; prevailing tenants recover costs and reasonable attorney’s fees. Each month a violation of section 98.1103(b) exists or continues, and each residential rental property for which a landlord uses an algorithmic device, is a separate and distinct violation.
rules.interaction: The ordinance states that its remedies are cumulative and in addition to any other remedies in the Division or at law, statute, or ordinance.
rules.quoted_span: It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
